# 4. Partial observability and zero-trust belief

## 4.1 World state is not directly available

The true world state `s_t in S` is only partially observed:

\[
o_t \sim Z(\cdot\mid s_t)
\]

HFO maintains a belief state. Because evidence can be incomplete or contradictory, the safest object is often a **credal set** rather than one precise probability distribution:

\[
B_t \subseteq \Delta(\mathcal S)
\]

A large/non-singleton `B_t` represents explicit uncertainty.

## 4.2 Evidence items

An evidence item is:

\[
e=(\text{claim},\text{value},\text{source},\text{grade},t_v,t_\tau,\text{provenance})
\]

where:

- `t_v` is valid time;
- `t_tau` is transaction/observation time.

## 4.3 Evidence precedence is a partial order

HFO uses an evidence order `preceq_E`, approximately:

\[
\text{chat}
\prec
\text{Slack/discussion}
\prec
\text{checkpoint}
\prec
\text{current projection}
\prec
\text{independent RESULT/VERDICT/ACT}
\prec
\text{exact provider/world/byte readback}
\]

This is not the claim that every higher source is always semantically correct. It means a lower projection may not silently override a newer exact higher-grade observation.

## 4.4 Belief update

Belief revision is:

\[
B_{t+1}=\mathsf{Update}(B_t,O_{t+1},E_{t+1},\preceq_E)
\]

When evidence is incompatible and no admitted reducer can resolve it:

\[
B_{t+1}=\text{UNKNOWN or a non-singleton hypothesis set}
\]

not a convenient invented scalar truth.

# 5. Hierarchy, holons, HIVE and PREY

## 5.1 Recursive scopes

Let `H` be a rooted hierarchy or acyclic scope graph. Each holon `h` has:

\[
\mathcal H_h=(B_h,I_h,Q_h,D_h,M_h,\pi_h)
\]

A child is locally autonomous only inside the parent's constraints:

\[
\operatorname{Authority}(h_c)\subseteq\operatorname{Authority}(h_p)
\]

and its output must satisfy the parent interface.

This gives HFO its fractal/8^N property without requiring one giant context.

## 5.2 Strategic HIVE loop

At a strategic scope:

\[
\mathsf{HIVE}:
\text{Hindsight}
\rightarrow
\text{Insight}
\rightarrow
\text{Validated Foresight}
\rightarrow
\text{Evolve}
\]

Mathematically:

\[
\theta_{t+1}=
\mathsf{Evolve}
\left(
\theta_t,
\mathsf{Validate}
\left[
\mathsf{Forecast}(B_t,M_t)
\right],
F_t
\right)
\]

where `theta` is the current policy/mechanism repertoire.

## 5.3 Tactical PREY loop

For one bounded worker transition:

\[
\mathsf{PREY}:
\text{Perceive}
\rightarrow
\text{React}
\rightarrow
\text{Execute}
\rightarrow
\text{Yield}
\]

Yield must emit an externally sufficient state delta:

\[
Y_t=\sigma(W_t,C_t,a_t,o_{t+1},r_t)
\]

such that the next carrier does not require hidden conversational continuity.

## 9.1 WorkItem type

A WorkItem is:

\[
w=(job,id,phase,state,input,key,route,owner,effect,accept,next,retry,deadline)
\]

It defines one bounded legal transition and its acceptance contract.

## 9.2 Eligibility

A WorkItem is eligible iff:

\[
\mathsf{eligible}(w,t)=
[state(w)=READY]
\land
[dependencies(w)\;satisfied]
\land
[capacity(w)\;available]
\land
[WIP\;limit\;allows]
\]

If there is no eligible work:

\[
Q_t^{eligible}=\varnothing
\Rightarrow
N_{\text{new workers}}=N_{\text{model requests}}=0
\]

This is the formal prevention of false metabolism.

## 9.3 Pull selection

A basic deterministic pull policy is:

\[
w^*=\arg\max_{w\in Q_t^{eligible}}
(priority(w),-ready\_time(w))
\]

subject to role/capability compatibility.

## 9.4 Lease/fence invariant

For an idempotency key `k`:

\[
\#\{\lambda:\lambda.key=k\land\lambda.active\}\le1
\]

and:

\[
\#\{e:e.key=k\land e.accepted\}\le1
\]

The realistic target is not magical exactly-once physical execution. It is:

- at-most-one accepted canonical effect;
- idempotent or compensated external effects;
- stale fence losers perform zero accepted effect.

# 10. Candidate generation, verification and acceptance

## 10.1 Candidate generation

A stochastic worker produces:

\[
y\sim K_{c,\ell}(\cdot\mid w,\kappa)
\]

The output is only a candidate:

\[
y\in\widetilde{\mathcal Y}
\]

not canonical state.

## 10.2 Verification vector

Let verification be a vector:

\[
V(y,w)=
(V_{mechanical},V_{semantic},V_{authority},V_{provider},V_{human},V_{economic})
\]

The required subset depends on consequence class.

## 10.3 Acceptance

Canonical admission is:

\[
\mathsf{Admit}(y,w)=1
\iff
\mathsf{HardGates}(y,w)
\land
\mathsf{RequiredVerification}(y,w)
\land
\mathsf{Readback}(y,w)
\]

No receipt means no accepted transition:

\[
\neg\mathsf{Receipt}(y)\Rightarrow\mathsf{Admit}(y,w)=0
\]

## 10.4 Producer/verifier separation

For consequential work:

\[
producer(y)\neq verifier(y)
\]

A producer may run self-checks, but may not grant final promotion to itself.

## 10.5 Evidence-path independence

Let `P_y` be the provenance DAG for a verdict. A minimally independent verdict requires at least one evidence path from source/provider/mechanical observation to verdict that is not controlled by the producer:

\[
\exists p:\;source\leadsto verdict
\quad\text{such that}\quad producer\notin p
\]

Model-family plurality without independent evidence can remain correlated and is not world truth.

# 11. Event sourcing, temporal DAGs and songlines

## 11.1 Canonical state is a fold over accepted events

Let:

\[
E_t=(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_t)
\]

be accepted append-only events. Then:

\[
X_t=\mathsf{fold}(\delta,X_0,E_t)
\]

where `delta` is the deterministic state reducer.

A GitHub body/current file may be a cached projection of this state, but stale projection cannot outrank newer accepted event receipts.

## 11.2 One epoch is a DAG

For each activation epoch `t`, define a directed graph:

\[
G_t=(V_t,E_t^{same})
\]

with:

\[
G_t\;\text{acyclic}
\]

The usual path is:

\[
Observation\rightarrow Belief\rightarrow Selection\rightarrow WorkItem\rightarrow
Execution\rightarrow Candidate\rightarrow Verify\rightarrow Reduce\rightarrow Receipt
\]

Feedback is legal only across epochs:

\[
Receipt_t\rightarrow Observation_{t+1}
\]

\[
Memory_t\rightarrow Belief_{t+1}
\]

\[
Fitness_t\rightarrow MOME_{t+1}
\]

This prevents same-epoch self-authentication.

## 11.3 Category-theoretic interpretation

Define a category `C_HFO` where:

- objects are typed accepted system/work states;
- morphisms are verified transitions with receipts;
- composition is exact handoff;
- identity morphisms are legitimate no-op/yield transitions.

For:

\[
f:x\rightarrow y,
\qquad
g:y'\rightarrow z
\]

composition `g∘f` is defined only when:

\[
y\equiv y'
\]

under exact type, input identity and hash/provenance requirements.

Unverified LLM outputs live in a proposal graph/category and do not become canonical morphisms until admitted.

A **songline** is therefore an ordered path of verified anchors/morphisms:

\[
Seed\rightarrow Role\rightarrow Intent\rightarrow WorkItem\rightarrow Gate\rightarrow
Transition\rightarrow Receipt\rightarrow NextAnchor
\]

If an anchor is stale or missing, the path is broken and the actor yields/blocks rather than inventing the missing edge.

# 12. Topological / sheaf interpretation of the COP

This section is optional mathematics, but it captures HFO's contested partial observations well.

Let a cover `{U_i}` represent overlapping scopes observed by different actors/sensors. A presheaf `F` assigns local claims/state to each scope:

\[
x_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)
\]

Local views are compatible on an overlap iff:

\[
x_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=x_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}
\]

If all local sections are compatible, they can glue to a global section/COP:

\[
\exists x\in\mathcal F(\cup_i U_i)
\]

If they do not agree, HFO must preserve the obstruction:

\[
\nexists\;\text{consistent global section}
\Rightarrow
UNKNOWN\;|\;CONTRADICTION\;|\;NEEDS\_REDUCER
\]

not force a false global narrative.

This is the mathematical form of:

- no single agent sees everything;
- overlapping reports must reconcile on shared facts;
- Byzantine/conflicting claims remain explicit;
- the COP is a constructed, source-bound object rather than one model's story.

No sheaf library is required to implement this principle; an evidence graph with typed overlap checks may suffice.

# 13. Memory: CoALA × trust lattice × bitemporal state

## 13.1 Memory atom

A memory atom is:

\[
m=(id,type,trust,claim,sources,t_v,t_\tau,supersession,verification,canary)
\]

Functional type:

\[
type\in\{episodic,semantic,procedural,working\}
\]

Trust/promotion state:

\[
trust\in\{bronze,silver,gold,quicksilver,quarantine,museum,graveyard\}
\]

## 13.2 Memory cannot define current authority

\[
\boxed{Memory\;evidence\neq Current\;authority}
\]

A memory that something worked before cannot authorize the same action now without fresh WorkItem/authority/capability state.

## 13.3 Retrieval

A retrieval function produces a bounded activation bundle:

\[
\kappa=R(id_i,w,M_t,\beta)
\]

where `beta` is a byte/token budget.

The bundle should contain:

- tiny Gold invariants;
- current Quicksilver authority/work state;
- relevant semantic atoms;
- relevant episodic scars/outcomes;
- triggered procedural Skills/gates;
- explicit excluded stale/conflicting items;
- UNKNOWNs.

## 13.4 Memory fitness

A memory system is useful only if retrieval changes behavior correctly:

\[
J_M=
\Delta P(\text{correct bounded action}\mid\kappa)
-
\lambda P(\text{stale/contradictory retrieval})
-
\mu C_{retrieval}
\]

A database full of embeddings but never consumed by the next actor has near-zero operational memory capacity.

## 15.1 Genotype, loadout and phenotype

Let:

- `g` = durable genotype/contract;
- `ell` = model/tool/skill/substrate loadout;
- `xi` = stochastic variation.

Then:

\[
p=\mathsf{Render}(g,\ell,\xi)
\]

The same genotype can yield heterogeneous phenotypes across Claude, GPT, Gemini, different tools or different prose realizations.

## 15.2 Descriptors, objectives and constraints

For phenotype `p`:

\[
d(p)\in\mathbb R^k
\]

is the behavior descriptor, and:

\[
f(p)\in\mathbb R^m
\]

is the objective vector, subject to:

\[
h_j(p)\le0
\]

for all hard constraints.

## 15.3 Archive update

For archive cell `cell(d(p))`:

\[
A_{t+1}[cell(d(p))]
=
Pareto
\left(
A_t[cell(d(p))]\cup\{p\}
\right)
\]

This retains diverse survivors instead of prematurely collapsing onto one scalar champion.

## 15.4 External/protected promotion

Long-term ecological promotion requires protected or external fitness:

\[
\text{internal model preference alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{ecological champion}
\]

For books, reader behavior and contribution economics eventually dominate model votes. For runtime architecture, forced-death, race, empty-queue and operator-zero assays dominate elegant prose.

# 19. Regrowth, quines and minimum description length

Let:

- `K` = reconstruction seed/germline pointers;
- `L_t` = live provider/repo/world bindings;
- `D` = deterministic reconstruction decoder.

A reconstructed system is:

\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_t=D(K,L_t)
\]

Regrowth passes when it is observationally equivalent to the current system on required invariants and next legal edge:

\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_t\equiv_{\mathcal I}\mathcal H_t
\]

A practical Kolmogorov/MDL seed objective is:

\[
K^*=\arg\min_K
\left(
|K|+\lambda C_{retrieval}(K)
\right)
\]

subject to:

\[
P(\text{cold regrowth pass across heterogeneous carriers}\mid K)\ge1-\epsilon
\]

This is a practical engineering minimality target, not a proof of true Kolmogorov complexity.

A poetic self-description without reconstruction tests is heritage, not an operational quine.
